title: Graphs and Greedy Proximity Search: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Graphs and Greedy Proximity Search: Visual Guide

1. Postings To Adjacency | Bridges postings lists (term -> documents) to adjacency lists (vertex -> nearby vectors); a three-way switch renders the same five-vertex graph as an adjacency matrix, an adjacency list and CSR offsets/neighbors arrays, while a slider scales the corpus from 1,000 to 10,000,000 vectors and prices each representation | The matrix is O(n^2) - 125 GB of mostly absent edges at a million vectors - while the list is O(|V|+|E|); retrieval traversal enumerates neighbors, so flat CSR arrays of 32-bit IDs win.

2. Walk To The Query | Steps the worked traversal from entry A(0,0) to F(9,8) against query (9,9), computing every distance live (12.73, then B 7.81 vs C 8.06, then D 2.83 vs E 5.83, then F 1.00), with a 'score all 6' toggle for the exact-scan comparison | Greedy moves only on strict improvement and stops when no neighbor beats where it stands; it never proves an unvisited vertex is farther, which is why graph search is approximate.

3. Scan Or Walk | Four sliders - corpus n, vertices visited v, degree M and dimension d - drive side-by-side bars of exact O(nd) versus graph O(vMd) multiply-adds and the bytes moved at 4 bytes per dimension (768 dims = 3,072 bytes per vector) | The graph wins exactly when v*M is much smaller than n; push the visit budget or degree up and the advantage is capped away, because the win is a ratio and not a property of graphs.

4. Trapped At Four | The number-line local minimum - A at 0, C at 4, B at 6, D at 9.8, query at 10 - with a candidate-queue-width slider (k=1 is pure greedy) and a toggle that adds a bridge edge B-D, tracing every expansion and what it kept or dropped | Greedy halts at B because both A (10) and C (6) are worse than 4, so reaching D needs a worsening step; breadth (k >= 2) or a bridge edge fixes it, and the failure belongs to the graph, not the distance metric.

5. Highways Then Streets | Ten base clusters with a sparse upper layer of representatives at clusters 1, 3, 5 and 8; toggles for base-only, layered and a weak bridge between clusters 3 and 4, plus a slider for how many clusters an upper link reaches | At reach 4 the search jumps 1 -> 5 -> 8, descends and walks locally to 9.8; long links give reach, local edges give precision, and layering shortens the path without making the search exact.
